name: Louis Mountbatten, 1st Earl Mountbatten of Burma
role: British admiral; last Viceroy and first Governor-General of India (1947–48); First Sea Lord and Chief of the Defence Staff
summary: A British naval officer and member of the royal family who oversaw the transfer of power in India, brought the date forward, and presented the 1947 partition plan on the ground that majority communities should not be coerced. He urged princely states to join India or Pakistan. As a retired defence chief he argued in 1979 for reducing nuclear armaments and said the arms race had no military purpose.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Wikipedia reports that in 1969 he tried to persuade the Spanish pretender Infante Juan to abdicate to ease Juan Carlos's accession, and discussed with Nixon the position of Juan Carlos and Constantine II of Greece. This is action for monarchies, not a stated view.

right-to-secede.rationale: He drove the 3 June 1947 plan under which areas with a majority of one community could separate, on the stated ground that they should not be coerced. He also told the princely states they could not remain independent, so the principle was applied only to the provinces.

political-violence-never.rationale: Inferred: from his 1947 statement that the country could not afford any toleration of violence, said in the context of communal violence at partition. The principle is broader than the context he addressed.

military-superiority.rationale: In 1979 he said peace was best preserved by a military balance of strength between East and West, to be based on mutual restraint rather than ever-increasing armaments, not by superiority.

national-self-determination.rationale: He advanced the date of the transfer of power and handed sovereignty to India and Pakistan, and in the 1947 broadcast rejected coercing communities against their will. He did not extend this to princely states seeking independence.

force-without-un.rationale: Wikipedia reports he strongly advised Eden in 1956 against seizing the Suez Canal, arguing it would undermine the UN and divide the Commonwealth. Reported secondhand.

consent-of-governed.rationale: In 1947 he argued communities should not be made to live under a government they did not accept; in his 27 October 1947 letter on Kashmir's accession he said the question should be settled by a reference to the people.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: A historian's post on Mountbatten reports that he favoured closer European integration for Britain. Secondhand.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Inferred: from his work in NATO and his Atlanticist outlook as described by a historian; he never proposed ending alliances.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Mixed record: he drove Polaris, but a historian's post reports he shared the view that an independent deterrent was a comfort blanket disguising geopolitical reality. Secondhand and not a direct statement.

collective-defense.rationale: Inferred: from his service as chairman of the NATO Military Committee and a historian's account that he supported an Atlanticist policy.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: In his 3 June 1947 broadcast he said there could be no question of coercing large areas where one community has a majority to live against their will under a government dominated by another community, and the only alternative to coercion was partition. Said of India, not as a general rule.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Wikipedia reports that, urging princes to accede on defence, external affairs and communications, he stressed the instruments left them all the practical independence they needed.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Inferred: from his driving the end of British rule in India and his support for decolonisation in south-east Asia; a historian describes him as not an imperial nostalgist.

elective-rulers.rationale: Inferred: from his 1969 and 1970 efforts to secure hereditary succession in Spain and to support the Greek monarchy, as reported by Wikipedia.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Inferred: from his chairmanship of the NATO Military Committee and a historian's account of him as an Atlanticist.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Inferred: from his 1969 effort to have Infante Juan step aside so that his son Juan Carlos could succeed to the Spanish throne, as reported by Wikipedia.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Inferred: in the 1947 broadcast he said he first urged leaders to accept the 1946 Cabinet Mission plan, which he called the best arrangement for the interests of all communities and which preserved a united India under shared arrangements.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Inferred: from his opposition to the 1956 Suez operation, as reported by Wikipedia, and his statement that in a nuclear war there would be no winners. Not a general statement of his view on defensive war.

arms-reduction.rationale: In his Strasbourg speech of 11 May 1979 he said that by reduction of nuclear armaments it should be possible to achieve greater security at a lower level of military confrontation, and called the nuclear arms race purposeless.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Mixed record: he was described as the driving force behind Britain's Polaris submarine deterrent, yet in 1979 he said he could see no use for nuclear weapons that would not end in escalation and urged mutual restraint and reduction. He did not address unilateral disarmament.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: In his letter of 27 October 1947 accepting Kashmir's accession he wrote that it was the government's wish that, once order was restored and the invader cleared, the question of accession should be settled by a reference to the people.

notes:
Most statements are null because his recorded words concern the transfer of power, princely states and nuclear arms. His Polaris advocacy as First Sea Lord and his later opposition to nuclear use in 1979 point different ways, so the nuclear-weapons answers are 0 at low confidence. The Kashmir plebiscite letter was written as Governor-General on his government's behalf.

Merged with an independent claude-haiku-5-5 audit: 3 answers taken from it, 12 agreed, 0 conflicts settled by the integrator.

claude-haiku-5-5 notes: Only the 1979 Strasbourg speech and the 1947 broadcast are his own words in the sources opened. Suez, the Spanish and Greek succession efforts and the Kashmir plebiscite and UN referral come from secondary accounts, rated medium at most. Wikipedia and Wikiquote were checked, but neither gives his stance on Rhodesia, Kenya, Cyprus, Northern Ireland, the welfare state or the economy, so those stay null. The Wikipedia article says the Viceroy's 1947 date was brought forward to 15 August; this measure is not recorded as an answer to any statement. Sources on Kashmir are partisan and are not used for inclusion. The 'brink of the final abyss' line is taken from the speech text itself.
